Work in /opt/nxeon. Write the definitive internal manual for **Nxeon**, a Hostinger-style VPS hosting platform (Next.js App Router + Prisma/Postgres + systemd worker + Proxmox + Mailcow). A previous attempt at this produced nothing, so start fresh.

YOU OWN: `docs/DOCUMENTATION.md` and new files under `docs/`. Do NOT edit `docs/AUDIT-24H.md`, `docs/QA-PRELAUNCH.md`, `docs/MIGRATION-FIELD-NOTES.md` — read them, they are goldmines. Do NOT edit ANY source file. Eight other agents are changing code concurrently, so describe what you read and cite where you read it.

RENDERING TARGET — read `app/admin/docs/page.tsx` and `lib/markdown.ts` FIRST:
- Rendered at `/admin/docs`; the viewer **splits at every `##` (H2)** into a searchable section list, so H2s ARE the navigation. Choose them as things someone would search for.
- Supported: headings, bold, italic, inline code, fenced code blocks, lists, blockquotes, links, rules, and **GitHub tables** (table support was added recently — use them freely).
- NOT supported: mermaid, images, raw HTML, nested lists (they render flat — restructure instead).
- So draw every diagram, screen layout and workflow as **ASCII/box art in fenced code blocks**, under ~100 columns.

PRODUCE:
1. Preserve the existing dated change-log entries; restructure so reference material leads and the history sits in a clearly-marked later part.
2. Front section: what Nxeon is; architecture ASCII diagram (web / worker / Proxmox / Postgres / Mailcow / nginx); request and job lifecycles; environments (prod `/opt/nxeon`, staging `/opt/nxeon-staging`).
3. Per-feature chapters. Each: what it does, ASCII wireframe of the customer screen, ASCII workflow, code entry points as real `file:line`, data model touched, failure modes, how an admin diagnoses it. Cover: deploy wizard; plans/terms/pricing; wallet, checkout, the wallet/card split; invoices; **renewals + card auto-charge + dunning** (`worker/billing.ts` — wallet credit first, card for the remainder, retries days 1/3/5, `Server.suspendReason` UNPAID vs ABUSE vs ADMIN and why it exists); server lifecycle ops; resize and **proration** (`lib/proration.ts` — one shared function so displayed = charged = credited); disk expansion; volumes; backups (daily, keep 3, `/tank/backup/platform` separate from customer archives, restore verification); snapshots/restore; **server migration** — the flagship, deepest chapter, including the verification gate and `COMPLETED_WITH_ISSUES`; control panel; web console; SFTP; domains and transfer-in; Cloudflare OAuth; SSL lifecycle; Nxeon Mail; business email + DKIM; game servers; Build with AI; teams; support; notifications; API tokens; 2FA (note `lib/totp-verify.ts` is a PLAIN module on purpose — exported from a `"use server"` file it was a public brute-force oracle); growth; bandwidth; admin surfaces; RBAC.
4. Admin runbooks: deploying; restarting safely (**never restart the worker while a job is RUNNING** — show the queue check); reading worker logs; diagnosing a stuck job; re-running a failed migration; issuing a cert by hand; checking mail deliverability — including the `/etc/hosts` + `nsswitch: files myhostname dns` trap that makes the system resolver answer reverse lookups from a local file, so deliverability checks MUST query authoritative nameservers; rolling back.
5. Troubleshooting: symptom → cause → fix tables mined from the field notes and both audits.
6. Data model reference from `prisma/schema.prisma`.
7. **A "known gaps / not true yet" section.** The audits catalogue features that are saved-but-unread, simulated, or unreachable. Documenting a gap honestly is worth far more than describing an aspiration as fact — overclaiming is this codebase's dominant defect class and the docs must not add to it.

METHOD: investigate before writing; every `file:line` must be real; never invent behaviour. If unsure, read it; if still unclear, write what you verified and flag the gap.

HARD CONSTRAINTS
- Documentation only. Do NOT edit source. Do NOT run `npm run build`/`dev`, do NOT restart services, do NOT git commit/push. Read-only DB inspection is fine.

Report: the H2 structure, roughly how much you added, and anything documented-but-wrong you corrected.

1	# Nxeon — VPS hosting platform
2	
3	Hostinger-style VPS hosting platform running on this Proxmox VE 9 dedicated server (OVH KS-GAME, i7-7700K, 64GB RAM, 2×450GB NVMe ZFS mirror + 4TB HDD backup pool).
4	
5	## Architecture
6	
7	- **Web panel**: Next.js 15 (App Router, server actions) + Tailwind v4, served by `nxeon-web.service` on port 3000, behind nginx on port 80. Public IP: 51.79.162.96.
8	- **Worker**: `worker/index.ts` run by `nxeon-worker.service` (as root — it manages iptables). Polls the `Job` table every 3s and executes provisioning/lifecycle jobs against the Proxmox API.
9	- **DB**: PostgreSQL 17, database `nxeon`, Prisma ORM ([prisma/schema.prisma](prisma/schema.prisma)). Use `npm run db:push` after schema changes.
10	- **Proxmox**: API token auth (`nxeon@pve!platform`, creds in `.env`). Templates: VMID 9000 (Ubuntu 24.04), 9001 (Debian 13), cloud-init based, cloned onto ZFS storage `vmdata`.
11	- **Networking**: VMs attach to NAT bridge `vmbr1` (10.20.0.0/24, gateway .1). IPs allocated from 10.20.0.100–250 ([lib/ipam.ts](lib/ipam.ts)). SSH exposed via DNAT port forwards 20000–29999 in iptables chain `NXEON_FWD`, rebuilt from DB by [worker/network.ts](worker/network.ts) — never edit that chain by hand.
12	- **Cloud-init**: vendor snippet at `/tank/backup/snippets/nxeon-vendor.yaml` (installs qemu-guest-agent, enables root password SSH).
13	
14	## Portals & design system
15	
16	- Customer portal (`app/dashboard/**`) and admin ops portal (`app/admin/**`) are separate sidebar apps sharing `components/portal/Shell.tsx` (sidebar, topbar, notifications bell, ⌘K command palette backed by `/api/search`).
17	- Design system lives in `app/globals.css` (glass cards, gradient buttons, navy palette) + `components/ui/primitives.tsx` + `components/ui/charts.tsx` (dependency-free SVG charts). Use these — do not add chart libraries.
18	- Admin impersonation: `impersonateUser()` sets a signed cookie; `currentUser()` returns the target, `realUser()` the actual admin; banner + exit handled in Shell. Admin pages call `realUser`/`requireAdmin` and refuse to render while impersonating.
19	- Metrics come from Proxmox RRD via `/api/metrics` (node for admins, per-server for owners).
20	
21	## Integrations (activate via /opt/nxeon/.env)
22	
23	- **Stripe**: `STRIPE_SECRET_KEY` + `STRIPE_WEBHOOK_SECRET` → wallet top-ups switch from demo gateway to Checkout (`/api/stripe/checkout`, webhook `/api/stripe/webhook`, event `checkout.session.completed`, idempotent by session id).
24	- **Namecheap** (`lib/namecheap.ts`): `NAMECHEAP_API_USER/KEY/USERNAME/CLIENT_IP` (+`NAMECHEAP_SANDBOX=1` for testing) → domain search/register/renew/DNS management. TLD retail prices in `TLD_PRICES`.
25	- **GitHub**: remote `origin` = `git@github.com:santino1233/nxeon.git` via deploy key `/root/.ssh/nxeon_deploy`. Every commit auto-pushes via `.git/hooks/post-commit`. `.env`/credentials are gitignored — never commit secrets.
26	
27	## Conventions
28	
29	- All state changes to VMs go through `Job` rows — the web app never calls Proxmox mutation endpoints directly (read-only status calls are OK).
30	- One in-flight job per server (enforced in `serverAction`).
31	- Admin-only actions live in [lib/actions.ts](lib/actions.ts) and must call `requireAdmin()`.
32	- Free VPSes: `Server.isFree = true`, no billing, `expiresAt = null`.
33	- Wallet amounts are integer cents.
34	
35	## Documentation — keep it current (required)
36	
37	- **Every change, fix, or addition MUST update `docs/DOCUMENTATION.md` in the same commit.** Add a dated bullet to §15 (Change history) and edit any section the change affects (data model, subsystems, feature catalog, integrations, roadmap, etc.). A commit that changes behaviour without touching the docs is incomplete.
38	- Keep `ROADMAP.md` in sync too: check off / move the item you completed.
39	- `docs/DOCUMENTATION.md` is the single source of truth. The public mirror at `https://revsports.ca/docs` is regenerated from it with `node scripts/publish-docs.mjs` (zero-dep markdown→styled-HTML renderer → `/var/www/nxeon-docs/index.html`) — run that after editing the doc so the hosted page matches. The `/docs` nginx location lives in `scripts/configure-domains.sh` so it survives vhost regeneration.
40	- The claude.ai artifact webpage (`https://claude.ai/code/artifact/9b0c97f5-4c34-4f89-bee9-b5a80eb23892`) can only be updated from an interactive Claude Code session (headless/cron runs can't reach it) — that refresh is best-effort, the repo doc + `/docs` page are authoritative.
41	
42	## Commands
43	
44	- Build: `npm run build` (must pass before restarting services)
45	- Deploy after changes: `npm run build && systemctl restart nxeon-web nxeon-worker`
46	- Worker logs: `journalctl -u nxeon-worker -f`
47	- E2E test: `npx tsx scripts/e2e-test.ts` (orders a real VM; delete it afterwards via a DELETE job)
48	- Admin credentials: `/root/nxeon-credentials.txt`
49	
50	## Domains & TLS
51	
52	- **Single source of truth**: `/etc/nxeon/domains.env` (BASE_DOMAIN, ADMIN_HOST, STAGING_HOST, CERTBOT_EMAIL). The domain is a placeholder (`revsports.ca`) until the real one is bought. **Never hardcode the domain anywhere in app code** — the app uses `APP_URL` / `NXEON_ADMIN_HOST` from `.env`, and nginx vhosts are generated.
53	- **To migrate to a new domain**: edit `/etc/nxeon/domains.env`, point DNS (A records for apex, www, admin host, staging host) at the server, then run `scripts/configure-domains.sh`. It regenerates nginx vhosts, obtains Let's Encrypt certs, updates APP_URL in both `.env`s, and restarts web. That's the whole migration.
54	- **Routing**: customer portal on `https://BASE_DOMAIN` (admin path returns 404 here — hidden); admin ops portal on `https://ADMIN_HOST` (secret subdomain, root 302→/admin); staging on `https://STAGING_HOST`. HTTP→HTTPS 301. Real LE cert (auto-renews via certbot timer); self-signed fallback for bare-IP.
55	- Secure cookies are on (`COOKIE_SECURE=1`) now that real HTTPS exists. Stripe webhook is live at `https://BASE_DOMAIN/api/stripe/webhook`.
56	
57	## Environments
58	
59	- **Production**: `/opt/nxeon`, DB `nxeon`, services `nxeon-web` (port 3000) + `nxeon-worker`, nginx port 80, VPS pools IP 10.20.0.100–250 / SSH ports 20000–29999, NAT chain `NXEON_FWD`. Public: http://51.79.162.96
60	- **Staging**: `/opt/nxeon-staging`, DB `nxeon_staging`, services `nxeon-staging-web` (port 3001) + `nxeon-staging-worker`, nginx port 8080, ISOLATED VPS pools IP 10.20.0.50–99 / SSH ports 30000–30999, NAT chain `NXEON_FWD_STG`, VM tag `nxeon-staging`. Public: http://51.79.162.96:8080. Admin creds: `/root/nxeon-staging-credentials.txt`.
61	- Instance differences are driven entirely by `.env` (NXEON_ENV, NXEON_COOKIE_NAME, NXEON_NAT_CHAIN, NXEON_TAG, NXEON_IP_START/END, NXEON_SSH_PORT_START/END, NXEON_CRED_FILE, PORT, APP_URL) — the code is identical.
62	- **Deploy flow**: push to GitHub → `scripts/deploy-staging.sh [ref]` builds+migrates+restarts staging → verify at :8080 → `scripts/promote-production.sh` rebuilds+restarts production. The improvement agent should test changes on staging before promoting.
63	
64	## Safety rules
65	
66	- NEVER touch VMIDs 9000–9999 (templates) except to add new templates.
67	- Staging and production share the Proxmox node but never overlap: staging only ever allocates IPs .50–.99 and ports 30000–30999. Never point staging pools at production ranges.
68	- Test risky/provisioning changes on staging (`scripts/deploy-staging.sh`) before promoting to production.
69	- Never `qm destroy` a VM that has a `Server` row — always go through a DELETE job.
70	- Do not commit `.env`. Do not print the Proxmox token into logs or docs.
71	- Always `git commit` working states; never leave the tree broken — services restart from this directory.
72

1	# Customer Migration — Field Notes & Failure Catalog
2	
3	Real-world failures observed running the lift-and-shift migration against a live
4	customer server, with the fix for each. **This is the acceptance criteria for the
5	migration engine**: a customer should be able to migrate, point DNS, and have their
6	site serve over HTTPS with no server access.
7	
8	Source of truth for these findings: a real migration on 2026-07-25 from a
9	HestiaCP/Hostinger box (Debian, nginx 1.25, 72.62.69.9) to a fresh Nxeon VPS
10	(Ubuntu 22.04, nginx 1.18, 1 vCPU / 2 GB / 25 GB).
11	
12	---
13	
14	## The architectural lesson
15	
16	**Do not blind-copy the source's `/etc/nginx` (or `/etc/apache2`) tree.** That single
17	behaviour caused roughly half of the failures below. Copying wholesale imports the
18	source's `nginx.conf`, its include layout, its panel-specific vhosts, its IP
19	bindings, and its certificate paths — none of which are valid on the target.
20	
21	Instead:
22	1. **Parse the source vhosts for intent** — server_name(s), document root or upstream
23	   proxy target, port, TLS on/off.
24	2. **Generate clean configs for the target's own web-server version.**
25	3. Leave the target's `nginx.conf` and include layout **intact**.
26	4. Copy the source config tree to a reference dir only
27	   (`/root/nxeon-migrations/<id>/source-nginx/`), never into live config.
28	
29	---
30	
31	## Failure catalog
32	
33	### Web server / routing
34	
35	| # | Failure | Symptom | Fix |
36	|---|---------|---------|-----|
37	| 1 | Source `nginx.conf` overwrote the target's | `include sites-enabled/*` disappeared → a generated vhost is **silently ignored** | Write vhosts where the *live* `nginx.conf` actually includes; verify with `nginx -T \| grep <server_name>`, not just `nginx -t` |
38	| 2 | Hardcoded source IP in ~21 configs | `bind() to <old-ip>:80 failed (99)` — nginx won't start | Rewrite source IP → target IP everywhere, or generate configs without IP binding |
39	| 3 | `/etc/letsencrypt` not migrated | 5 vhosts referenced missing certs + `options-ssl-nginx.conf` → config test fails → **web server down** | Migrate `/etc/letsencrypt` (certs, renewal conf, accounts) **or** strip TLS blocks and re-issue via certbot after DNS points over. Never leave a config referencing a missing cert |
40	| 4 | Web-server version mismatch | `http2 on;` (nginx ≥1.25) is an unknown directive on 1.18 | Detect target nginx version; translate/neutralise incompatible directives |
41	| 5 | Missing log directories | `open() "/var/log/apache2/domains/..." failed` | `mkdir -p` + `touch` every log path a config references before testing |
42	| 6 | Dead catch-all default server | Copied `listen <ip>:80 default; proxy_pass http://<ip>:8080;` hijacked everything → **502 on all traffic** | Detect copied default/catch-all servers whose upstream is dead; disable them |
43	| 7 | `listen` specificity beats `server_name` | An IP-bound block (`listen <ip>:80`) wins over generic `listen 80` regardless of server_name — our vhost never selected. **Repeated on 443** → wrong cert → `ERR_CERT_COMMON_NAME_INVALID` | Generated vhosts must bind the target's public IP explicitly on **both** 80 and 443 when copied configs do |
44	| 8 | Stale nginx PID after config swap | `invalid PID number "" in /var/run/nginx.pid`; `reload` fails | Use `restart` (not `reload`) after replacing nginx.conf; verify `systemctl is-active` |
45	| 9 | Multi-tenant wildcard subdomains | Tenant subdomains hit no server block → wrong cert | Add `server_name *.<domain>` when the app is multi-tenant (e.g. a `*_BASE_DOMAIN` env var). **A wildcard cert needs DNS-01** — HTTP-01 cannot issue `*.domain` |
46	
47	### Application startup
48	
49	| # | Failure | Symptom | Fix |
50	|---|---------|---------|-----|
51	| 10 | Docker **images** not migrated | Standalone containers using locally-built images (`app/frontend:latest`, never in a registry) can never start | `docker save \| gzip` on source → stream → `docker load` on target. Prefer `docker pull` for public-registry images |
52	| 11 | App configured for the **old domain** | `PUBLIC_APP_URL`/`PUBLIC_API_URL` pointed at the old host — and frameworks like Astro/Next **bake the API URL into the static bundle at build time**. Page loads; nothing works | Detect old-hostname references in copied env; offer to rewrite **and rebuild** the affected image. A frontend calling the old server's API is a *silent* failure |
53	| 12 | Secrets in a non-standard env file | compose had `${VAR}` placeholders but no `.env` — real file was `prod.env` (used via `--env-file`) | Detect the env file the project actually uses; if placeholders would resolve empty, **refuse to start** and name the missing vars |
54	| 13 | Absolute binary paths differ between hosts | Migrated systemd units called `/usr/local/bin/node` (manual install on source); target has `/usr/bin/node` (apt) → unit crash-looped **880 times** | Resolve `ExecStart` binaries; symlink or rewrite the unit to the target's real path |
55	| 14 | Framework build artifacts don't transfer | Next.js `.next` copied but had no valid production build → `Could not find a production build` | Detect framework apps and run their build on the target (`next build`), or verify `BUILD_ID` exists before enabling the service |
56	| 15 | MySQL users & grants not migrated | Dump intentionally skips the `mysql` system schema, so **app DB users vanish** → access-denied despite data being present | Enumerate non-system users, `SHOW GRANTS`, replay `CREATE USER`/`GRANT` on the target preserving password hashes. (Postgres `pg_dumpall` already carries roles) |
57	| 16 | Stack-manager deployments | Apps deployed via Dokploy/Coolify/Portainer keep env/secrets in the manager's **own database**, not on disk (`/data/compose/<id>/`) | Detect the layout and warn explicitly — file copy alone will miss the secrets |
58	
59	### Storage / capacity
60	
61	| # | Failure | Symptom | Fix |
62	|---|---------|---------|-----|
63	| 17 | `/var/lib/containerd` is a **separate store** from `/var/lib/docker` | Relocated `/var/lib/docker` to the attached volume; root **still** hit 100% — containerd had grown to 9.4 GB | Relocate/bind-mount **both**; add to `/etc/fstab`; verify with `df -h /var/lib/docker /var/lib/containerd` |
64	| 18 | Build cache is enormous | `docker builder prune -af` reclaimed **7.1 GB** after two builds | Prune after bring-up; retry once after pruning on ENOSPC before failing |
65	| 19 | Attached block volume unused | A 20 GB volume was attached but unformatted/unmounted while root filled | Detect an attached disk with no FSTYPE/mountpoint; format ext4, mount persistently by UUID, relocate the container stores onto it |
66	| 20 | Space estimate ignored Docker overhead | Guardrail estimated the ~11 GB file copy; image pulls/builds blew past it → `no space left on device` killed 2 of 3 compose projects | Include source image bytes + 1.5–2× build/ingest headroom; **re-check free space before the image phase**, not only at start |
67	| 21 | Small targets get starved | On 1 vCPU / 2 GB, a .NET + Astro build starved the box so hard the **QEMU guest agent stopped responding** | Don't assume the guest agent stays reachable during builds; keep the engine's SSH channel authoritative. Warn when target resources are small relative to detected workload |
68	
69	---
70	
71	## Verification bar
72	
73	The final summary must distinguish **"migrated & running (verified)"** from
74	**"copied — needs a manual step"**, and verification must **HTTP-probe the real
75	hostname(s)** — not merely check that a port is listening. Never report success when
76	the site does not actually serve.
77	
78	Where full automation is genuinely impossible, say so **actionably** — name the file,
79	the value, and the command:
80	- wildcard TLS certs (need DNS-01),
81	- compiled-in API URLs (need a rebuild),
82	- stack-manager secrets held in the manager's database,
83	- standalone containers whose images aren't reproducible.
84	
85	---
86	
87	## Same-OS question
88	
89	Matching the source OS removes a real class of problems (web-server/package version
90	and config-syntax incompatibilities — items 4 and some of 13), and the wizard
91	recommends it. **It is not a silver bullet**: items 1, 2, 3, 6, 7, 10, 11, 12, 14,
92	15, 17–21 are OS-independent migration-completeness issues.
93	
94	---
95	
96	## 2026-07-25 — "reported SUCCESS, customer saw a certificate warning and an Apache default page"
97	
98	A real customer migration completed and reported success. The customer opened their
99	main site and got a browser certificate warning, clicked through it, and landed on
100	the **Apache2 Debian Default Page**. Six of their domains were dark. The run log
101	said `Sites actually serving: 4/4`.
102	
103	Five separate failures, all now closed in `worker/migrate-real.ts`.
104	
105	| # | Failure | Symptom | Fix (implemented) |
106	|---|---------|---------|-------------------|
107	| 22 | **The success metric could not fail** | Log line 1: `Sites actually serving: 4/4`. 2	
3	Audit of the engineering session transcript `4f329df3-66ee-49c8-a6c5-615ecf189efc.jsonl`
4	(2026-07-23 09:56 → 2026-07-25 19:58 UTC; the 24-hour window requested by the user is

7	live codebase at `/opt/nxeon`** (HEAD `8e93b13`, `origin/main` in sync).
8	
9	The standard applied throughout: *code existing is not the same as the feature working.* A server
10	action nobody calls, a status computed and then overwritten by its caller, a flag that silently
11	switches a real integration into simulation — all count as **NOT DONE**, regardless of how complete
12	the implementation looks.

16	## Executive summary
17	
18	### Counts
19	
20	| | User instructions | Assistant recommendations | Total |
21	|---|---|---|---|
22	| **DONE** | 40 | 17 | **57** |
23	| **PARTIAL** | 14 | 8 | **22** |
24	| **NOT DONE** | 6 | 18 | **24** |

27	| **Totals** | **61** | **47** | **108** |
28	
29	Headline: the *feature* work of the last 24 hours largely landed. What did not land is the
30	**trust layer** — the places where the platform tells a paying customer something that is not true.
31	Nine of the top ten gaps below are of that kind, and three of them move real money.
32	
33	### CRITICAL — found during this audit, ranks above everything below
34	
35	**Any customer can take over another customer's email domain, reset the password on their live
36	mailboxes, and then read and send mail as them.** This was surfaced by a QA agent still running from
37	the original session (`docs/QA-PRELAUNCH.md`) and I verified the whole chain independently:
38	
39	1. `lib/actions-email-hosting.ts:254-256` — the "one subscription per domain" check is scoped to the
40	   **caller**: `where: { userId: user.id, domainName: name, … }`. It never asks whether another user
41	   already holds that domain.
42	2. `prisma/schema.prisma:604` — `EmailSubscription.domainName` is a plain `String` with **no
43	   `@unique`**, so the database does not stop it either. `Mailbox.address` (`:623`) is likewise not
44	   unique.
45	3. `lib/actions-email-hosting.ts:491-538` `addMailbox` checks only `sub.userId !== user.id`, and its
46	   duplicate check (`:514`) is scoped to *that subscription's own* mailboxes. The attacker can
47	   therefore create `admin@victim.com` under their own subscription. No DNS-verification gate applies.
48	4. `lib/actions-email-hosting.ts:684-707` `resetMailboxPassword` validates
49	   `mailbox.subscription.userId !== user.id` — which **passes**, because the row is the attacker's —
50	   and then calls `mcSetMailboxPassword(mailbox.address, password)` (`:707`). Mailcow keys mailboxes
51	   by **address**, so this sets the password on the victim's real, live mailbox. The new password is
52	   returned to the attacker (`:721`).
53	
54	Cost of the attack: the price of the cheapest email plan. Impact: full read/send access to another
55	customer's business email, plus a denial of service (the victim is locked out). **This must be fixed
56	before any customer is onboarded** — the minimum fix is a global uniqueness check plus `@@unique` on
57	`EmailSubscription.domainName` and `@unique` on `Mailbox.address`, and requiring domain ownership or
58	completed DNS verification before any mailbox operation.
59	
60	### Top 10 gaps, in priority order
61	
62	1. **Stripe confirm/webhook race — customer charged, service never delivered.**
63	   `app/api/stripe/webhook/route.ts:21` credits the wallet on `checkout.session.completed`.
64	   `app/api/stripe/confirm/route.ts:27` then gets `credited === false` (P2002 replay guard in
65	   `lib/stripe.ts:242`) and **skips** `placeOrder` (`:32`), `applyResize` (`:54`) and
66	   `applyDiskExpand` (`:78`), falling through to a bare redirect. `STRIPE_WEBHOOK_SECRET` is set in
67	   `.env`, so the webhook is live and this race is reachable today. The customer pays, the money
68	   lands in their wallet, the server is never provisioned / the resize never applied / the disk
69	   never grown — **silently, with no error**. Fulfilment must key off its own idempotency record,
70	   not off the wallet-credit flag.
71	
72	2. **SSL issuance is simulated on production and reports success.**
73	   `worker/ssl.ts:303` gates real certbot on `ENABLE_REAL_SSL === "1"`. That variable is **not set
74	   in `/opt/nxeon/.env`** (only `ENABLE_REAL_MIGRATION` and `ENABLE_REAL_CPANEL` are). Production
75	   therefore falls to `worker/ssl.ts:319-335`, which writes `status: "ACTIVE"`, a fabricated
76	   `expiresAt = now + 90d`, and notifies the customer *"Your Let's Encrypt certificate is active."*
77	   No certificate exists on the box. `components/customer/SslManager.tsx:204` renders that fake
78	   expiry as fact. There is also no renewal sweep (`SslCertificate.autoRenew` is written by
79	   `lib/actions-ssl.ts:121` and read by nothing).
80	
81	3. **Renewals have no card auto-charge — good-card customers get suspended.**
82	   The user asked for this explicitly at 19:06 ("credit cards need to be primary payment method for
83	   auto charged"). `worker/billing.ts:134` debits the wallet only; `:192-214` suspends after grace.
84	   `User.stripeCustomerId` / `stripePaymentMethodId` (`prisma/schema.prisma:135-136`) are **never
85	   written and never read**. No `off_session`, no `SetupIntent`, no `setup_future_usage` anywhere.
86	   Six dunning templates exist (`lib/mailer.ts:340-473`) with exactly **one** call site — the admin
87	   preview page. The engine was scoped and agreed, not built.
88	
89	4. **The migration result card still says "Migration complete 🎉" in green when the migration
90	   left domains dark.** This is the precise bug the 19:46 verification gate was built to kill, and
91	   it survived one layer up. `components/customer/MigrationWizard.tsx:1331` computes `withIssues`,
92	   then `:1332` folds it into `done`, and `:1352` + `:1368-1370` render the emerald progress bar and
93	   the "Migration complete 🎉" card for `COMPLETED_WITH_ISSUES` identically to a clean run. Only the
94	   small `StatusDot` is amber. Separately, the honest per-step summary written to
95	   `Migration.items.results` (`worker/migrate.ts:190`) is **never read by any UI** — the customer
96	   sees only an 8 000-char log tail.
97	
98	5. **Game-server settings apply is simulated on production and claims success with no caveat.**
99	   `worker/game-config.ts:39` requires `ENABLE_REAL_GAMECFG === "1"`; it is unset. The simulated
100	   branch (`:76-97`) stamps a marker and notifies *"Game settings applied on `<hostname>` — Minecraft
101	   (vanilla) settings were applied."* — the `(sandbox)` qualifier is appended only when
102	   `NXEON_SANDBOX` is set, which it is not in production. Nothing touches the VM.
103	
104	6. **Volume detach has no safety check, and the confirmation says the opposite.**
105	   `lib/actions-volumes.ts:147-164` guards only on status; `worker/volumes.ts:236` yanks the disk out
106	   of the VM config with no unmount or in-use probe. `components/customer/Volumes.tsx:172` tells the
107	   customer *"Detach … Data is preserved."* — which is false for a volume carrying `/var/lib/docker`,
108	   the exact configuration the migration engine creates (`worker/migrate-real.ts:227`, `:1323-1371`).
109	   Safe-detach was recommended three times in-session and never built. (The *reinstall* guard **was**
110	   built and is real — `worker/index.ts:428-448`.)
111	
112	7. **Backups: a customer's manual backup can delete the platform's own VM backups, and a paid
113	   add-on does nothing.** `lib/proxmox.ts:413-429` prunes by `vmid` across the whole `backup` PVE
114	   storage — the same `/tank/backup` that `scripts/backup-vms.sh:31-35` writes platform backups into.
115	   Separately, the deploy wizard sells **"Daily backups"** (`components/customer/DeployWizard.tsx:209`),
116	   stores it as `addons.dailyBackup` (`lib/order.ts:183`), and **nothing ever reads it** to set
117	   `Server.autoBackup` (default `false`, `prisma/schema.prisma:342`). A customer who ticks that box
118	   gets no scheduled backups. Pruning also only ever runs on the success path of a *new* backup — no
119	   standalone retention sweep exists.
120	
121	8. **Coupon codes on card top-ups are accepted, promised, and silently ignored.**
122	   `components/customer/CouponField.tsx:60-66` renders *"Code X applied — 20% bonus … Bonus is
123	   credited when you add funds."* and writes an `nxeon_coupon` cookie. That cookie is read in exactly
124	   one place — `lib/actions.ts:527`, inside the **demo** gateway that hard-refuses in production. The
125	   real card top-up (`app/api/stripe/checkout/route.ts:26-42`) has no `discounts`, no
126	   `allow_promotion_codes`, and `creditCheckoutSession` credits `amount_total` verbatim.
127	
128	9. **No email is sent for any billing failure, suspension, or termination.**
129	   `grep -rn "sendMail" worker/*.ts` returns **zero** matches. `worker/billing.ts:205-212` and
130	   `:423-449` write in-app `Notification` rows only. `emails.suspended` and `emails.serverTerminated`
131	   are referenced solely by `app/admin/email-templates/page.tsx`. A customer whose server is
132	   suspended for non-payment gets a bell icon in a portal they are no longer logging into. 29 of the
133	   33 catalog templates have no sender at all.
134	
135	10. **The migration engine's TLS ladder is unreachable in production because the caller drops three
136	    of its inputs.** `worker/migrate.ts:156-167` calls `runRealMigration` with only
137	    `{migration, target, items, report}` — never `cloudflareToken`, `acmeEmail` or `knownDomains`
138	    (declared at `worker/migrate-real.ts:182-184`). Consequences: rung 3 (DNS-01 wildcard via the
139	    customer's connected Cloudflare) can **never** fire even for customers who have connected
140	    (`:2967`, `:2988`); every certificate is issued `--register-unsafely-without-email` (`:2831-2833`)
141	    so no expiry warnings ever arrive; registered `Domain` rows are excluded from the published set.
142	    And `issueMigrationCertificates` (`worker/migrate-real.ts:3097`) — the documented "call again
143	    after DNS moves" entry point — **has zero callers**, so TLS is never retried after cutover.
144	
145	Runners-up, all real but below the line: off-site backups are inert
146	(`scripts/backup-offsite.sh:27-31`, `/etc/nxeon/backup-offsite.env` has no target set); Proxmox
147	`:8006` and host SSH are open to the internet (`scripts/firewall.nft:28,33`); no migration rehearsal
148	harness exists; `ROADMAP.md` is misleading in both directions; tax is configured and never charged.

293	
294	```

296	MigrationWizard.tsx:1332   const done = row?.status === "DONE" || withIssues;

1	# Nxeon — Pre-launch QA audit
2	
3	**Date:** 2026-07-25 · **Scope:** customer portal, admin portal, backend (`lib/**`, `worker/**`, `app/api/**`)
4	**Method:** source review, read-only inspection of the live `nxeon` database, `npx tsc --noEmit`, and
5	cross-checking the Proxmox perl source on this host. Nothing in this audit modified code, services, or data.
6	
7	---
8	
9	## Executive summary
10	
11	### The single most dangerous issue
12	
13	**Any customer who can afford the cheapest email plan can take over another customer's email domain,
14	reset the password on their live mailboxes, and read and send mail as them.**
15	
16	`lib/actions-email-hosting.ts:254-257` scopes the "one subscription per domain" check to the *caller*:
17	
18	```ts
19	const dupe = await db.emailSubscription.findFirst({
20	  where: { userId: user.id, domainName: name, status: { not: "CANCELLED" } },
21	});
22	```
23	
24	There is no check that another user already holds that domain, no `@@unique` on
25	`EmailSubscription.domainName` (`prisma/schema.prisma:604`), no `@unique` on `Mailbox.address`
26	(`:623`), and no `sub.verified` gate on any mailbox mutation. Every Mailcow call is keyed by the
27	**address string** on one shared Mailcow instance, so `resetMailboxPassword` (`:706`) rewrites the
28	password of whatever real mailbox that string names — and hands the plaintext back to the caller.
29	
30	Mailcow is configured in production (`MAILCOW_API_URL` + `MAILCOW_API_KEY` are both set), and the live
31	DB holds two active subscriptions with real mailboxes — including `admin@revsports.ca`, the platform's
32	own `BASE_DOMAIN`, which receives Nxeon's own password-reset mail. This is exploitable today, by any
33	signed-up user, in three clicks. Full detail in **P0-1**.
34	
35	### Go / no-go
36	
37	**NO-GO for paying customers.** Fix P0-1 through P0-8 first; they are the launch blockers.
38	
39	This is not a verdict on the codebase's quality — much of it is genuinely better than typical for this
40	stage. The wallet ledger is atomic and race-safe (`lib/wallet.ts` conditional `updateMany`, CAS on
41	`expiresAt` in every renewal path). Ownership checks are present and correct on **all 20+ mutating
42	server actions and all 35 API routes** — two independent passes found no IDOR in the server/domain/
43	volume/website/database/file surfaces. `lib/ssh-exec.ts` is a reject-don't-sanitize allowlist with
44	mandatory timeouts and secrets confined to STDIN; **no command injection was found anywhere**, and
45	that was looked for hard. Disk shrink is blocked at four independent layers. `qm destroy` is reachable
46	only through a `Server` row. Job claiming is atomic. GDPR deletion re-validates server-side.
47	
48	The problems are concentrated in four themes:
49	
50	* **9 P0s.** One live cross-tenant email takeover; one unauthenticated 2FA-verification endpoint; two
51	  paths that silently destroy customer volumes; a Stripe flow that can take money and provision
52	  nothing; proration that overcharges by up to $379; refunds that are untraceable and non-idempotent;
53	  a suspension path that permanently deletes a *paid-up* customer's VM; and a "Daily auto-backups"
54	  add-on that never produces a single backup.
55	* **A large "furniture" surface — the dominant defect class in this codebase.** ~18 admin settings are
56	  written to the DB and read by nothing (the dunning controls, the referral reward, the domain markup —
57	  which displays 0% while customers are charged 25%), and the customer portal has a matching set:
58	  notification preferences, SSL auto-renew, WHOIS privacy, custom nameservers, registrar lock, team
59	  permissions, affiliate tiers, mail Reply-To and the API `write` scope are all persisted, all
60	  confirmed with a green "Saved", and all read by nothing. **Every one of these tells the user a
61	  guarantee is in force when it is not.**
62	* **Whole features that cannot work today**: plan downgrades (blocked by a guard no live plan pair can
63	  satisfy), coupons (redemption UI hidden whenever Stripe is on), bandwidth metering (and therefore the
64	  entire abuse-detection subsystem built on it), 4 of the 5 one-click apps, and game settings.
65	* **One availability landmine**: a single hung job wedges the entire platform's queue, forever.
66	
67	A useful signal for triage: the team already knows how to handle an unfinished feature correctly.
68	`components/customer/AutoRecharge.tsx` is deliberately **not rendered**, with the reason documented in
69	`app/dashboard/billing/page.tsx:11-15` — *"the feature is unwired … so we don't expose it and promise
70	something that does nothing."* That is exactly the right call. Roughly 25 findings below are the same
71	situation handled the other way.

1152	# P2 — error paths and hardening
1153	
1154	1. **No irreversible destroy is confirmed server-side.** Every destroy relies on a browser
1155	   `window.confirm`; the action takes a bare id — `lib/actions.ts:445-485` (`delete`/`reinstall`),
1156	   `lib/actions-volumes.ts:167` (`deleteVolume`), `lib/actions-server-lifecycle.ts:81`
1157	   (`reinstallToOs` — the "type ERASE" gate is client-only at `components/customer/ReinstallOs.tsx:39`),
1158	   `lib/actions-server.ts:66` (`rollbackSnapshot` — no status check, no confirmation),
1159	   `lib/actions-databases.ts:168`, `lib/actions-websites.ts:295`. Next.js validates the Origin header
1160	   on server actions so this is not remotely exploitable; the impact is accidental/scripted invocation
1161	   with no server-side "are you sure", no soft-delete, no undo. Note the **admin** delete requires
1162	   typing the hostname (`components/admin/ServerAdminActions.tsx:52`) — the customer's own irreversible
